checks: Cold-read the frozen proof and checked the cited source candidate 26455afca6af9c16 §5 (10)–(12) and final paragraph; source bytes match the declared digest. The frozen claim extracts the interpolation identity, not any unproved existence of a deepest face or separator.

The accepted canonical energy support is available at any sampled own-interior mark, including at a relative-boundary base, and extends on C by density of each own interior. For the volume support, if K contains c+r B_d and d_H(K,L)=h then L ⊆ K+h B_d ⊆ c+(1+h/r)(K-c). Applying this both ways bounds |v(K)-v(L)| by (h/r) times the common upper bound for volume roots. This proves the relative-base Lipschitz property when combined with canonical Hausdorff Lipschitz continuity.

Concavity of v follows from canonical Minkowski inclusion and Brunn–Minkowski. The infimal convolution of the convex function -v restricted to the compact base hull with L times the norm is finite and convex and equals -v on the hull; a whole-affine-span subgradient supplies T even on its relative boundary, including the singleton case.

Weighted AM–GM yields the majorant including F=0. At Y it equals one after normalization. Its own slope is (d/N) times (N/d) a_Y, which is a_Y; independently grad_y log H = (1/N) grad_y log E = a_Y, and the mass normalization is constant in y. On all C, S≥0 and T≥v_min give the claimed floor. The volume bounds from inner and outer radii give v_min/v_max ≥ r/R, and the exact own denominator has floor 1/N.

At a positive interior interpolation all F_i and v_i are positive. Equality in H forces equality in both component inequalities by strict coordinate monotonicity. Writing the geometric mean as v(F/v)^(d/N) and normalizing by weights proportional to lambda_i v_i proves that equality also forces constant F_i/v_i. Energy equality in the containing-fiber form gives marked homothety under the actual convex inclusion.

Each affine-majorant gap is nonnegative and their positive-weighted sum vanishes. Dividing the common positive majorant at each contact by its value there gives a normalized upper support; the availability of both signs of each own-interior direction forces its continuous slope to be grad_y log H(Y_i)=a_{Y_i}.
